summary: Two brick range towers in Lake St. Clair, built 1855 to 1859 to guide ships through the South Channel; discontinued in 1934 and kept up since 1989 by a volunteer group.

corrections.proposed: Front light active again, flashing white every four seconds (LighthouseFriends); rear range not an active aid (USLHS). Needs checking against the Coast Guard Light List before the record changes.
corrections.why: The brief's 'inactive' covers both lights; the sources read give different status for the front light.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS 'Year Discontinued: 1907' is the first discontinuance. LighthouseFriends records re-establishment on 27 August 1915 and a final discontinuance in 1934, which matches the record's 1934 deactivation.

The rear range is not an active aid (USLHS). LighthouseFriends says the front light is an active aid again. Both are recorded in the story; the front light's status should be checked against a current List of Lights.
LighthouseFriends puts the lights 0.7 miles west of the southern tip of Harsens Island; the Save Our South Channel Lights history says just off the southeastern tip. The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends calls the rear tower cylindrical; the USLHS record says conical. The story gives both.
The Save Our South Channel Lights history says the keeper's house was taken down in the early 1930s; LighthouseFriends says it was torn down around 1934. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: 1) Front light status: LighthouseFriends says it is again an active aid, flashing every four seconds, The USLHS record is for the rear range and says not active. The brief says inactive. The story reports the LighthouseFriends claim as such. 2) Front tower lean: LighthouseFriends has the 1873 survey and the 1874 rebuild; SOSCL and the Wikipedia lead say the lean began in 1875. Unresolved; both dates are in the story. 3) Appropriations: LighthouseFriends gives $10,000 (1853) and $20,000 (3 Aug 1854). Wikipedia's lead gives $45,000 in 1856 (not cited). Only LighthouseFriends is cited. 4) Tower shape of the rear light: LighthouseFriends says cylindrical, USLHS says conical; the record's structure type reflects LighthouseFriends. 5) Roster matched by name, with the USLHS position 2.2 km from the station's coordinates. The roster is the USLHS place 'Saint Clair Flats South Channel Range Rear' and may cover both towers. 6) Name variants: LighthouseFriends prints 'George W. Warner', 'Goerge Watson', 'John Lane', 'Anson Badger'; the roster's forms are used. 7) Six people named Warner appear on the roster (Edward B., George, Stephen A., Willis S., Caroline M., Albert H.). The roster does not give family ties; none are asserted. 8) Lighthouse Board reports for 1853-1889 are not in the local corpus (the Lighthouse Board volumes start in 1891). The early history rests on LighthouseFriends. 9) The Commissioner list entry (scan page 143) is in a list whose heading was not read; the story says only that the list includes the range. 10) The 1871 canal range lights are a separate station (LighthouseFriends ID 847); not written here. 11) The NRHP form (Christensen, 1990, St. Clair Flats South Channel Range Lights, NRHP 90000853) is not digitised on NPGallery (placeholder only). Its contents are not used. 12) The US Coast Guard Historian's pages for the front and rear range: the archived copy returned only the Wayback index, so they were not used. 13) Access: the Michigan tourism listing says 'This is not open to the public' (read by WebFetch summary because fetch_text returned 403; not cached and not cited). The story's access statements rest on LighthouseFriends. 14) Newspapers were not searched for this station. 15) Founder Chuck Brockman is named only in his public role (SOSCL founder, per LighthouseFriends); personal details are left out. 16) Wikipedia was used only to find leads and is not cited. 17) Fact-check pass 2026-10-22: the Wikidata source (and its 'Fl W 4s' characteristic) was removed; the characteristic now rests on LighthouseFriends' 'white flash every four seconds'. 18) The rear tower shape and the dwelling's demolition date differ between sources and both are in the story. 19) The 1899 Board entry (scan page 218) says the front beacon was repointed and the rear range's dwelling and boathouse repaired; it is quoted from the volume, not from LighthouseFriends alone. 20) The Commissioner list entry (scan page 143) is printed under a heading the researcher did not read; the story says only that the list names the range.
